text:
Your agents have a voice now. 

 
 Heard ( heard.dev ) is the voice context layer for agents on macOS: text-to-speech for Claude Code and Codex. When your agent finishes, fails or needs your approval, Heard tells you in a sentence or two, so you can step away and still know what's going on.
 The engine in this repo is open source (Apache 2.0) and can speak locally with Kokoro text-to-speech , no account or API keys.
 

 
 Comparing macOS coding-agent notification tools? A sound or a banner tells you something happened. Heard tells you what happened: a spoken summary of the work itself, across every session and every agent. 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 heard.dev 
  · 
 Releases 
  · 
 Discord 
  · 
 Issues 
 

 

 What tools give AI coding agents a voice?

Heard (heard.dev) gives AI coding agents a voice: it speaks a short summary when Claude Code or Codex finishes, fails or needs your approval, and the open-source engine in this repo lets other command-line agents talk through heard run . The app needs macOS 14 or later, and heard run can only narrate what a process prints, so full-screen terminal interfaces may give it little to say.

 

 What is a voice layer for Claude Code?

A voice layer lets your coding agent talk to you, not only you to it. Claude Code's /voice covers the input half. Heard covers the output half: it follows the session and tells you out loud what changed, what failed and what needs a decision. The Heard app adds input too (on Power, press right ⌘ to talk to Parrot), so the whole loop can run by voice.

 Make Claude Code talk back, not just listen

Can you use text-to-speech with Claude Code? Yes. Claude Code's built-in /voice command is voice input: you talk and it types your prompt. Heard adds the other direction. Run heard install claude-code and Heard adds hooks (Stop, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit) to /.claude/settings.json , then speaks a short summary of what the agent did instead of reading the whole reply back. Voices come from local Kokoro (free, on your Mac) or your own ElevenLabs or Speechify key. Hooks return immediately, so Claude Code never waits on speech.

Want something smaller? Three single-purpose repos from the same team:

- claude-code-tts: text-to-speech for Claude Code and Codex, a free /say skill (MIT) that reads a short summary aloud with your computer's built-in voice. No API key, no account.
- claude-code-sound-notification: a sound or desktop notification when Claude Code finishes or needs your input (MIT, one install command).
- codex-sound-notification: a sound or desktop notification when OpenAI Codex CLI finishes a task or needs your approval (MIT, one install command).

 Add a voice layer to any command-line agent

To make any other command-line AI agent talk, put heard run in front of the command you normally use:

 

Heard starts the process under a PTY, passes its output through, and speaks what it prints. Quality depends on what the process emits: full-screen terminal interfaces may not give it enough to work with, and questions or approvals may still need the agent's own interface. Every wrapped command shares one session. heard run is part of this open source engine (see Self-host), not the Mac app. Claude Code and Codex don't need it: heard install claude-code and heard install codex give richer events. More in the docs.

 Open-source voice tool for coding agents that runs locally

The engine in this repo is open source under Apache 2.0 and needs no account or API keys. The voice runs on your Mac; the list below says exactly what can leave it:

- Speech comes from Kokoro text-to-speech on your Mac, after you run heard download-voice once (about 350 MB).
- With no Anthropic key and no Heard sign-in, spoken updates are built on your Mac from templates and the agent's own text. If the claude command is installed, the engine can send agent activity to Anthropic through claude -p , with your Claude login, to write rolled-up project summaries. An ambiguous reply to Heard's catch-up prompt can go the same way.
- Narration content and source code are never sent to analytics, which are on by default; turn them off by setting product analytics: false in the config file that heard config path prints.
- It speaks; it does not listen. Push to talk and voice replies are app features on Power.
- Add your own keys only if you want ElevenLabs voices or LLM-written summaries.

 

Full options in Self-host. Comparing local voice tools for coding agents? See open-source voice tools for coding agents.

 See and hear it run
🔊 Turn sound on for demo

 

 Get the app

The app is the managed experience: download, sign in, and you're narrating. Heard runs the cloud voices and the narration brain for you, with no keys to manage. Every new account starts with a 14-day Power trial, no card required. Prefer to run it yourself with your own keys? See Self-host.

The app also adds cloud agents like Grok Bot , Meta Muse , Devin, Manus and ChatGPT, and on Power you talk back.

Heard gives coding agents a voice. Heard (heard.dev) is the voice context layer for agents.

 Have your coding tool install it (recommended)

Paste this into Claude Code, Codex, or any AI coding tool:

 Install Heard so you can narrate your work to me out loud. Run: curl -L -o /tmp/heard.zip && unzip -o /tmp/heard.zip -d /Applications && xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Heard.app && open /Applications/Heard.app , then hand it back to me - a quick setup window opens and I'll take it from there.

 Homebrew

 

 Manual

Download Heard.dmg , drag Heard.app into /Applications , and open it. Setup walks you through sign-in, permissions and your voice.

 Works in every terminal

Heard listens to your agent, not your terminal, so narration works wherever the agent runs: Ghostty, Herdr, cmux, iTerm2, Terminal, Warp, WezTerm, tmux, VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed . Heard also knows where each session lives, so a jump back lands on the
